_comment: What the prompt explainer knows about programs, sites and ports. Programs are keyed by the file name of the executable; sites by domain suffix (the longest match wins). Plain words only: this text is shown to people who don't know what a port is.

browser.label: web browser
browser.allow: Websites and web apps open normally.
browser.deny: The site, or the part of a page that needs this address, won't load in the browser.

dns.label: name lookup service
dns.purpose: Turns names like example.com into the numeric addresses computers use. Almost every connection starts with one of these lookups.
dns.allow: Names keep resolving, so the internet keeps working.
dns.deny: Names stop turning into addresses: almost nothing on the internet will work.

time.label: clock sync
time.purpose: Keeps the computer's clock correct by asking a time server.
time.deny: The clock slowly drifts. If it drifts far, secure websites and logins start failing.

network.label: network manager
network.purpose: Connects you to Wi-Fi and wired networks and checks that the internet is really reachable (and whether a hotel or airport login page is in the way).
network.allow: Connections and the 'are we online?' check work normally.
network.deny: Wi-Fi may show limited connectivity, and login pages of public Wi-Fi may not appear.

packages.label: software installer and updater
packages.purpose: Downloads programs and updates, including security fixes.
packages.deny: Installs and updates fail, so you also miss security fixes.

firmware.label: firmware updater
firmware.purpose: Checks for and downloads updates for the computer's hardware (BIOS, docks, SSDs, mice).
firmware.allow: You are told about hardware updates.
firmware.deny: No hardware update checks. Nothing else breaks.

devtool.label: developer or command-line tool
devtool.purpose: Does what the command line asked: download a file, fetch code, log in to a server, install a library.
devtool.allow: The command you (or a script) ran finishes normally.
devtool.deny: That command fails with a connection error.

interpreter.label: script runner
interpreter.purpose: Runs a script or program written in a programming language. On its own it doesn't tell you much: what matters is which script it is running, shown under Advanced.
interpreter.allow: The script can reach this address. If you choose "from this executable", every script run by this program can, too.
interpreter.deny: The script fails to connect. Other scripts using the same runner are blocked as well if the rule covers the whole program.

chat.label: chat or calling app
chat.purpose: Sends and receives messages, calls and notifications.
chat.deny: Messages, calls or notifications stop arriving.

media.label: music or video app
media.purpose: Streams or downloads music and video.

games.label: game or game store
games.purpose: Downloads games and updates, signs you in and connects to game servers.
games.allow: Store, downloads and online play work.
games.deny: Downloads, sign-in or online play fail.

sync.label: file sync or backup
sync.purpose: Keeps files in step with other devices or a cloud service.
sync.deny: Files stop syncing, so devices fall out of step.

editor.label: code editor
editor.purpose: Edits code. It goes online for extensions, updates, language servers and AI features.
editor.allow: Extensions, updates and online features work.
editor.deny: Extensions or online features fail. Editing itself keeps working.

ai.label: AI assistant
ai.purpose: Sends your requests to an AI service and shows the answers.
ai.deny: The assistant can't reach its service and stops working.

vpn.label: VPN or private network
vpn.purpose: Builds an encrypted tunnel to another network.
vpn.deny: The VPN can't connect; traffic that relies on it fails.

local.label: local network service
local.purpose: Finds printers, speakers, TVs and other devices on your own network.
local.allow: Devices on your network show up.
local.deny: Printers, casting or shared drives on your network may not be found.

system.label: background system service
system.purpose: Part of the operating system that runs in the background.
system.allow: The service keeps doing its job.
system.deny: That part of the system can't do its online job; see the description above.

WebKitNetworkProcess.name: WebKit (built-in web view)
WebKitNetworkProcess.what: The network part of the web view other apps use to show web pages.

dnsmasq.name: dnsmasq
dnsmasq.what: A small name lookup and address-handing service.

dhcpcd.name: dhcpcd
dhcpcd.what: Asks the router for an address when you join a network.

pacman.name: pacman
pacman.what: Arch Linux's package manager: installs and updates the system's software.

yay.name: yay
yay.what: Installs and updates software from the Arch repositories and the AUR (community-made packages).

paru.name: paru
paru.what: Installs and updates software from the Arch repositories and the AUR (community-made packages).

reflector.name: reflector
reflector.what: Picks the fastest Arch download servers by testing them.

curl.name: curl
curl.what: A command-line tool that downloads or sends data to web addresses. Scripts and installers use it a lot.

git.name: Git
git.what: Fetches and sends code to code-hosting sites.

git-remote-https.name: Git
git-remote-https.what: The part of Git that talks to code-hosting sites over HTTPS.

ssh.name: ssh
ssh.what: Opens an encrypted remote login to another computer.

scp.name: scp
scp.what: Copies files to or from another computer over ssh.

uv.name: uv
uv.what: Downloads Python packages and Python itself.

cargo.name: Cargo
cargo.what: Downloads Rust libraries and builds Rust programs.

go.name: Go
go.what: Builds Go programs and downloads their libraries.

dockerd.name: Docker
dockerd.what: Runs containers and downloads their images.

podman.name: Podman
podman.what: Runs containers and downloads their images.

gradle.name: Gradle
gradle.what: Builds Android and Java projects and downloads their libraries.

nc.name: netcat
nc.what: A raw network tool that can send anything to any address. Normal for network testing; also a classic tool for remote shells.

ncat.name: ncat
ncat.what: A raw network tool that can send anything to any address. Normal for network testing; also a classic tool for remote shells.

socat.name: socat
socat.what: Connects network sockets and programs together; used for testing and tunnelling.

kdeconnectd.name: KDE Connect
kdeconnectd.what: Links your phone to the computer over your own network.

mpv.name: mpv
mpv.what: A video player. It goes online when you play a link instead of a file.

steamwebhelper.name: Steam (web part)
steamwebhelper.what: Draws Steam's store and library pages.

restic.name: restic
restic.what: Makes backups, often to a cloud store.

ollama.name: Ollama
ollama.what: Runs AI models on this computer. It goes online to download models.

opensnitch-ui.name: OpenSnitch window
opensnitch-ui.what: OpenSnitch's own window, the one asking you this.

avahi-daemon.name: Avahi
avahi-daemon.what: Announces this computer and finds printers, speakers and other devices on your own network.

smbd.name: Samba
smbd.what: Shares folders with other computers on your network.

geoclue.name: GeoClue (location)
geoclue.what: Works out where you are, for apps you allowed to know. It may look up nearby Wi-Fi networks online.

gvfsd-http.name: GVfs (file access)
gvfsd-http.what: Lets the file manager open web addresses as files.

goa-daemon.name: GNOME Online Accounts
goa-daemon.what: Keeps your linked online accounts (mail, calendar, cloud files) signed in.

evolution-source-registry.name: Evolution data service
evolution-source-registry.what: Syncs calendars and contacts for desktop apps.

xdg-desktop-portal.name: Desktop portal
xdg-desktop-portal.what: Lets sandboxed apps ask for files, screens and links.

colord.name: colord
colord.what: Manages colour profiles for screens and printers.

sshd.name: SSH server
sshd.what: Lets other computers log in to this one.

systemd.name: systemd
systemd.what: Starts and supervises everything else on the system.

Hyprland.name: Hyprland
Hyprland.what: The window manager that draws your desktop.

nireekshana.name: Bahya Nireekshana
nireekshana.what: This network monitor. It goes online to check for updates, run a speed test you started, or sync with your other devices.

githubusercontent.com.what: files and downloads stored on GitHub

archlinux.org.what: the system's software packages and news

googleapis.com.what: Google services that apps and websites use

cloudflare.com.what: a network that many websites run through

akamaiedge.net.what: a delivery network that carries files and video for many companies

akamaized.net.what: a delivery network that carries files and video for many companies

akamai.net.what: a delivery network that carries files and video for many companies

fastly.net.what: a delivery network many websites use

amazonaws.com.what: rented servers used by many different companies, so the owner alone says little about who you are talking to

cloudfront.net.what: a delivery network used by many different companies

azureedge.net.what: a delivery network used by many companies

windows.net.what: rented servers used by many companies

letsencrypt.org.what: checks that a website's security certificate is still valid

lencr.org.what: checks that a website's security certificate is still valid

digicert.com.what: checks that a website's security certificate is still valid

sectigo.com.what: checks that a website's security certificate is still valid

sentry.io.what: crash and error reports sent to the app's makers

segment.io.what: usage tracking for the app's makers

mixpanel.com.what: usage tracking for the app's makers

amplitude.com.what: usage tracking for the app's makers

app-measurement.com.what: usage tracking for the app's makers

datadoghq.com.what: usage and error reports for the app's makers

53.name: DNS
53.what: a name lookup (turning a name into an address)

443.name: HTTPS
443.what: an encrypted web connection: the network can see where it goes, not what it says

80.name: HTTP
80.what: an unencrypted web connection: anyone on the network path could read or change it

8080.name: HTTP (alternative)
8080.what: an unencrypted web connection, usually to a test or local server

22.name: SSH
22.what: an encrypted remote login or file copy

123.name: NTP
123.what: a clock check against a time server

67.name: DHCP
67.what: asking the router for an address

68.name: DHCP
68.what: asking the router for an address

5353.name: mDNS
5353.what: looking for devices on your own network (printers, speakers, phones)

1900.name: SSDP/UPnP
1900.what: looking for TVs, speakers and routers on your own network

3478.name: STUN
3478.what: setting up a voice or video call

19302.name: STUN
19302.what: setting up a voice or video call

25.name: SMTP
25.what: sending email directly to a mail server, which normal apps rarely do

143.name: IMAP
143.what: reading email over an unencrypted connection

9418.name: Git
9418.what: fetching code with Git's own protocol

22000.name: Syncthing
22000.what: syncing files with your other devices

_odd_ports: Ports remote-control and test tools default to. Only a hint: plenty of honest servers use them too.
